upload.geotiffUnsupported: GeoTIFF - CRS unsupported, using selected coordinates
upload.noGeoMetadata: No geo metadata - using selected coordinates
upload.noDataHelpWhat: Some elevation files mark the area outside their survey with a filler number instead of leaving it blank, and don't label it as such. Read literally it becomes flat terrain at that height, walled off from the real ground around it.
upload.noDataHelpFound: This upload has no labelled no-data value, but {value} fills {percent}% of it and sits well outside the real elevation range — so MapNG is treating it as empty. Where your tiles overlap it can then take the real ground from another tile instead of a hole.
upload.noDataHelpOverride: Leave this on Auto unless your data really does have terrain at {value} — a coastline at exactly 0 m, for instance. Then pick None.
upload.layersHelp: Your upload holds more than one survey. The top one is used wherever it has data; each one below fills what the ones above it left empty. Reorder them to change which survey wins where they overlap — newest first by default.
upload.gapFillStandardHint: Anything your layers don't cover comes from the global dataset, height-matched to your data at the seam.
upload.gapFillGpxzHint: Anything your layers don't cover comes from GPXZ, height-matched to your data at the seam.
upload.gapFillGpxzNoKeyHint: No GPXZ API key set — the global dataset will be used instead.
upload.gapFillNoneHint: Uncovered areas are interpolated from the edges of your data, not from a real dataset.

controlPanel.fetchesMaxDetail: - Fetches max detail (Terrain Z15, Sat Z17).
controlPanel.largeAreaRamWarning: Warning: Large area. May require high RAM.
controlPanel.processingResolutionHint: Enter any positive m/px value (up to 10 decimal places). Lower m/px means finer detail over a smaller area for the same output size.
controlPanel.processingResolutionCoverage: Covers {km} × {km} km at {px} px ({mpp} m per pixel)
controlPanel.processingResolutionCoverageTile: Each tile covers {km} × {km} km at {px} px ({mpp} m per pixel)
controlPanel.processingResolutionDetailUltra: very fine: for sculpting or painting terrain
controlPanel.processingResolutionGuide: 1 m per pixel suits most maps. Go lower (0.25–0.5) for finer terrain to sculpt or paint in game, over a smaller area. Go higher (2–4) to fit a very large area, with softer terrain and roads.
controlPanel.processingResolutionRange: Use a value between {min} and {max} m per pixel.
controlPanel.processingResolutionCoarse: At {mpp} m per pixel roads and small features come out coarse, and roads barely show in the 3D preview.
controlPanel.processingResolutionSuggest: The same area at 1 m per pixel: {px} px output with 1 m.
controlPanel.processingResolutionPickLarge: 2 m: twice the area, softer terrain
controlPanel.processingResolutionPickHuge: 4 m: very large areas, coarse terrain
controlPanel.rawTerrainOn: On: elevation and OSM roads are used exactly as downloaded. No smoothing, levelling, road curves or snapping. Bridges and tunnels are still built at export.
controlPanel.rawTerrainOff: Off: roads are smoothed and levelled into the terrain and their corners rounded. Turn on to keep your elevation data untouched.
controlPanel.overtureBuildings: Add missing buildings and heights from Overture
controlPanel.overtureBuildingsHint: OSM stays the source of buildings. Overture Maps adds a height to buildings OSM has none for, and the footprints OSM is missing (Microsoft and Google detected, national cadastres), as plain boxes in the default style.
controlPanel.osmCoverageHint: Inside the green outlines, OSM data loads from MapNG's own copy: fast, and unaffected by Overpass outages. Elsewhere it comes from Overpass.
controlPanel.customOverpassInvalid: Must be a full https:// address.
controlPanel.customOverpassHint: Paste your full Overpass URL including your key. Areas MapNG already hosts (Show MapNG OSM coverage) still load from MapNG's own copy, so your key is only used outside them; there it's tried first, with the public servers as backup. It stays in this browser only. Paid plans with Overpass access:
controlPanel.modeBasicHint: Just the BeamNG level. Switch to Advanced for heightmap, texture and 3D model downloads, Surrounding Tiles and more export options.
controlPanel.modeAdvancedHint: All tools: 2D and 3D asset downloads, Surrounding Tiles, per-category level options and preview extras.

disclaimer.title: Data Accuracy Disclaimer
disclaimer.lead: Please be aware that all terrain data, heightmaps, and 3D models generated by MapNG are estimations based on available satellite and elevation datasets.
disclaimer.resolutionBody: Heightmaps are exported using the selected processing resolution to keep scaling consistent in game engines. When using the Standard (30m) dataset, terrain is still upsampled, so it remains smoother and less detailed than native high-resolution sources like USGS or GPXZ.
disclaimer.usage: This tool is intended for modding and creative use. It should not be used for navigation, engineering, or critical real-world planning.

about.title: About MapNG
about.subtitle: Real-world maps for BeamNG.drive
about.hero: MapNG turns any real-world location into a playable BeamNG.drive level: terrain, textures, roads with markings and traffic signals, buildings, bridges, vegetation and more, built right in your browser.
about.whatBody: Pick a location, choose an elevation source, generate the terrain and check it in the 3D preview. Then export a complete BeamNG level ZIP built from real elevation and OpenStreetMap data, or take GeoTIFF and GeoJSON data into your own workflow. Batch mode processes whole grids of tiles and can stitch them into one large level.
elevationItems: Standard 30 m global (AWS Terrarium / SRTM), with roads smoothed and levelled automatically
USGS 1 m DEM (USA: CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii)
GPXZ premium (global high resolution, concurrent requests on paid plans)
Your own uploads: LAZ/LAS point clouds, GeoTIFF, ASC, GML/XML, layered and reprojected, with gaps filled from Standard or GPXZ and blended seams
previewItems: Satellite, OSM, hybrid and clay texture modes
3D buildings, trees, bushes and barriers from OSM
Mesh quality from low poly up to full native detail
exportItems: BeamNG level package (.zip), up to 16384 x 16384
GeoTIFF elevation (WGS84 or the source CRS)
Job data (.mapng): a complete saved session
Advanced mode and Batch mode (per tile) add: 16-bit heightmaps, satellite, OSM and hybrid textures, road masks, GLB, DAE and .ter
osmItems: MapNG's own OSM copy for the regions it hosts: fast, and unaffected by Overpass outages
Show MapNG OSM coverage outlines those regions on the map
Everywhere else: health-ranked Overpass mirrors with an edge cache
Bring your own Overpass server (Tracestrack, Overspan); MapNG's copy still answers first where it can
A banner tells you when the public Overpass servers are down
Overture Maps adds building heights and the footprints OSM is missing (on by default, under Include OSM Features)
If every Overpass server fails, OSM data comes from Overture Maps' monthly release instead, so exports still work
about.resolutionStrong: Output sizes from 512 to 16384 px at any processing scale (m/px).
about.resolutionBody: At 1 m/px that covers 0.26 km² up to 268 km². Standard 30 m elevation is upsampled and its roads are smoothed automatically; USGS, GPXZ, NMT and uploads keep their real detail.
about.batchIntro: Process large areas as a grid of tiles (up to 20 x 20). Each tile is generated in turn and its selected exports are packaged into its own ZIP. Features include:
batchItems: Combined BeamNG level: stitch a 2 x 2, 4 x 4 or 8 x 8 grid into one playable level (up to 16384 px)
Configurable grid size, resolution and export selection
Per-tile X/Y offsets with live drag editing on the map
Tiles Follow Map Center for center-anchored or world-locked layouts
Shared elevation baseline and a stitched 16-bit verification heightmap
Live progress with a color-coded tile grid and satellite thumbnails
Pause, resume and retry failed tiles; state survives a reload
GPXZ concurrent requests on paid plans
about.beamngBody: A ready-to-drive level ZIP for BeamNG.drive 0.40, built from the real place:
beamngItems: Terrain painted with materials from OSM land use, and a 2x satellite base texture you can touch up before export
A regional look chosen from the location: grass, ground cover, rocks and water
Regional trees from BeamNG's own models, picked from OSM tags and the local climate
Textured buildings with BeamNG's facades and roofs
DecalRoads with real surfaces, lane markings by country, crosswalks, stop bars, parking lanes and shoulders
Raised sidewalks with curb returns and ramps, and median islands on divided roads
Traffic signals for every approach, road signs, and street lamps that light up at night
Hydrants, bins, benches, utility poles and power lines
Bridges with solved decks, piers and graded abutments
AI traffic on the road network, road names on the minimap, and fuel stations
A surrounding backdrop and a detailed export_report.txt for troubleshooting
additionalItems: Run configurations: copy, paste, save and load
Job import/export: save and restore full sessions as .mapng files
Location search (Nominatim), preset scenic locations and Use my location
Keyless Esri satellite and topo layers with labels; your choices are remembered
Elevation overlay minimap of the selected area
Live progress with finished steps and timings for generation and export
Generation caching and cancel for long-running tasks
Light and dark mode, in 7 languages

tech.title: MapNG Tech Stack
tech.footer1: Built to assist with BeamNG.drive modding workflows.
tech.footer2: Open-source tooling for real-world terrain workflows.

core.name: Vue 3
core.desc: Composition API and reactive state management

core.name: JavaScript (ES6+)
core.desc: Modern standard with modules, async/await, and worker messaging

core.name: Tailwind CSS
core.desc: Utility-first styling with dark mode support

core.name: Vite
core.desc: Fast dev server and optimized production builds

core.name: Reactive Local State
core.desc: Pinia plus Vue refs/computed with localStorage persistence

render.name: Three.js
render.desc: WebGL 3D engine: geometry, materials, textures, export

render.name: TresJS
render.desc: Declarative Vue 3 renderer for Three.js scenes

render.name: Cascaded Shadow Maps
render.desc: 4-cascade CSM with 4096 px shadow maps and PCF filtering

render.name: HDR Environment
render.desc: 4K puresky HDRI for realistic ambient and reflection lighting

render.name: Collada and GLTF exporters
render.desc: BeamNG DAE shapes (buildings, bridges, sidewalks, power lines, backdrop) and GLB models in batch mode

map.name: Leaflet and Vue-Leaflet
map.desc: Interactive 2D map with keyless Esri satellite, topo and label layers, dark mode and OSM coverage outlines

map.name: proj4 and GeoTIFF
map.desc: CRS reprojection (incl. conic/UTM uploads), DEM parsing and GeoTIFF export

map.name: Local Transverse Mercator
map.desc: Custom metric projection for pixel-aligned processing grids

map.name: Nominatim Geocoding
map.desc: Dual-endpoint search plus reverse lookup for suggested BeamNG level names

tex.name: HTML5 Canvas API
tex.desc: Procedural texture generation up to 8192x8192 with OSM land-use, roads, and overlays

tex.name: fast-png
tex.desc: 16-bit precision heightmap and road mask encoding

tex.name: OSM Lane Renderer
tex.desc: Procedural road overlays, junction fills, crosswalk hints, and smoothed curves

tex.name: Web Workers
tex.desc: Off-thread terrain and image resampling with transferable buffers

src.name: AWS Terrain Tiles
src.desc: Global 30m SRTM elevation (Terrarium encoding at Z15)

src.name: USGS National Map
src.desc: 1m DEM via TNM Access API (CONUS, Alaska, Hawaii)

src.name: GPXZ API
src.desc: Premium global hi-res elevation with auto-chunking, rate-limit probing and concurrent requests for paid plans

src.name: Custom Elevation Upload
src.desc: Bring-your-own DEM: LAZ/LAS point clouds (laz-perf WASM), GeoTIFF (geotiff), ASC grids, and GML/XML (fast-xml-parser) - single or multi-tile, reprojected to the output grid

src.name: OpenStreetMap
src.desc: MapNG's own OSM archive on Cloudflare R2 (PMTiles, read by range), health-ranked Overpass mirrors with an edge cache, or your own Overpass server, with Overture Maps as a last resort

src.name: Overture Maps
src.desc: Building heights and footprints OSM lacks (Microsoft and Google detected, national cadastres), and all map data when OpenStreetMap's Overpass servers are down; from tiles.overturemaps.org (ODbL / CDLA)

src.name: JSZip
src.desc: Client-side ZIP packaging for BeamNG levels, batch jobs and .mapng sessions, streamed to disk (OPFS) for large levels

src.name: Blob URL Management
src.desc: Binary handling for large textures, heightmaps, and packaged exports

deploy.name: Cloudflare Workers
deploy.desc: Edge-hosted site and /api routes (OSM cache, OSM tiles from R2, proxies), deployed per branch by Workers Builds
